mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce discount rates and boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS level is positively correlated with 20-day forward returns (rank IC < 0.03) or the positive return rate in low-FEDFUNDS periods (FEDFUNDS < 1.5%) is not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 2.0%, it signals a monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of such instances, or the rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) and rising employment (PAYEMS month-over-month growth > 0.5%) indicates a strong labor market, which supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The condition (UNRATE<4.0% AND PAYEMS_mom_growth>0.5%) occurs, but 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of such instances, or the rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market contraction regime (HOUST < 1000 thousand units), economic weakness leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST < 1000 and 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of such instances, or the rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher industrial production index (INDPRO) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as stronger industrial activity signals robust economic growth.
failure_condition: The rank correlation between INDPRO and 20-day forward returns is negative (i.e., higher INDPRO is associated with lower returns) or the rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI (CPIAUCSL) rises above 2.5%, it signals accelerating inflation, which triggers monetary tightening and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of such instances, or the rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising GDP (GDPC1 month-over-month growth > 0.5%) and rising housing starts (HOUST month-over-month growth > 0.5%) indicates strong economic demand, supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The condition (GDPC1_mom_growth>0.5% AND HOUST_mom_growth>0.5%) occurs, but 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of such instances, or the rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.0%), the labor market is tight, supporting corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 4.0% and 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of such instances, or the rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
